chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah sets forth an example: a man with several partners who quarrel with one another, and a man wholly owned by one man. Are they equal in condition? He said: As for the one with quarreling partners, it is because the first one gathers the scattered [people] for his leadership, and while doing so, some curse each other and some distance themselves from each other. As for the man of peace [wholly owned], he is the first truly [in authority] and his Shias.

Then he said: The Jews differed after Musa (peace be upon him) into seventy-one sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy are in the Fire. The Christians differed after Isa (peace be upon him) into seventy-two sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy-one are in the Fire. And this Ummah differed after its Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) into seventy-three sects, seventy-two of which are in the Fire and one is in Paradise.

And from the seventy-three sects, thirteen sects claim our Wilayah and our affection; twelve of them are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. And sixty sects from the rest of the people are in the Fire.
ai.seo_question: How many sects will the Muslim community divide into according to Shia hadith, and which one is saved?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi contextualizes the Quranic parable of divided versus unified leadership by linking it to the historical fragmentation of major Abrahamic faiths and the specific eschatological division of the Muslim Ummah into seventy-three sects. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'Thirteen Sects' claiming Wilayah, distinguishing the single saved group (often identified as the Twelvers) from the twelve deviant ones, thereby establishing the criterion of authentic Wilayah as the key to salvation amidst sectarian diversity.
